conventions.convention: Inner products are linear in the first argument. Matrix units act by E_ij x = ⟨x,e_j⟩e_i, and dagger denotes the adjoint for this convention.
The Choi operator is the unnormalized sum J_B(Φ) = Σ_ij E_ij ⊗ Φ(E_ij), with the input factor first and output factor second; its chosen ordered orthonormal input basis is part of the definition.
A finite Kraus family may be empty, in which case it represents the zero map; zero operators are also permitted.
Channels are complex-linear completely positive maps that preserve trace on every input endomorphism. Zero-dimensional input and output spaces are allowed.
A Stinespring isometry has codomain K ⊗ E, with output K first and environment E second; the environment is the factor traced out.

Unitary conjugation is defined here for nonzero finite-dimensional spaces and surjective linear isometries. Its global-phase invariance concerns a single conjugation map and makes no controlled-operation assertion.

load_bearing.statement: For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces H,K, a fixed ordered orthonormal basis B of H, and complex-linear Φ:L(H)→L(K), complete positivity, non-negativity of J_B(Φ), and existence of a finite Kraus representation are equivalent.
For a finite Kraus representation Φ(X)=Σ_a K_a X K_a† between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, trace preservation on every input operator holds if and only if Σ_a K_a†K_a=I_H.
A complex-linear map between the full operator spaces of finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces that has a finite Kraus representation is completely positive.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces H,K, an ordered orthonormal basis B of H, and complex-linear Φ:L(H)→L(K), non-negativity of J_B(Φ) implies a finite Kraus representation with at most dim(H)dim(K) operators.
For a linear isometry V:H→K between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, V†V=I_H; if V is also surjective, VV†=I_K.

Every channel Φ:L(H)→L(K) between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces has a finite Kraus representation; for any such representation with N operators there are an N-dimensional environment E and a linear isometry V:H→K⊗E with Φ(X)=Tr_E(VXV†) for every X.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces H,K, a fixed ordered orthonormal input basis B, and complex-linear Φ:L(H)→L(K), being a channel is equivalent to each of: nonnegative J_B(Φ) with output partial trace I_H; a finite normalized Kraus representation; and a finite isometric Stinespring representation.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 first discusses the '(i,α),(j,β) entry' of the Choi operator and then says 'The same entry of Σ_a K_a E_ij K_a†'. The latter operator acts on K and has indices (α,β), rather than product indices (i,α),(j,β). The displayed coefficient calculation is correct, but the entry comparison is mistyped; it should compare that Choi entry with the (α,β) entry of the Kraus output.

seams_checked.note: The page summaries agree on the linear-first root pairing, ordered orthonormal coordinates, finite-dimensional scope, and zero-dimensional cases.
Complete positivity uses the supplier's ancilla-last block amplification for every integer r≥1. The Choi proof explicitly constructs the swap needed for input-first Choi order.
The example uses density operators only on nonzero C² and retains the supplier's nonnegative, trace-one definition and linear-first pairing.
Tensor maps, lexicographic product bases, zero factors, trace-pairing nondegeneracy, and second-factor partial trace are used with their stated domains and conventions.

The page declares this prerequisite, but its current item bodies contain no direct citation to an assigned channel item. Its expectation-estimation procedure explicitly requires a supplied finite unitary dilation and charges its access; it does not infer free circuit implementation from Stinespring existence.
The end-to-end contract explicitly uses full-operator CPTP maps on nonzero finite-dimensional spaces. Hybrid and tensor bounds cite precisely closure under composition and tensor products.

Cited interfaces are finite normalized Kraus representations, finite isometric dilations, product matrix-unit spanning, and isometry-plus-partial-trace channels. These follow from the assigned statements; taking the identity isometry supplies partial trace itself.

Instrument and coherent-record constructions use finite Kraus representations of finite-dimensional CP maps and their formulas on every operator. No efficient or freely available dilation is inferred.

Recovery and subsystem items faithfully use Kraus existence, full-operator CPTP definitions, adjoint-square normalization, and composition closure. The encoding conjugation is justified directly as a normalized one-operator Kraus map.
Channel-location schedules use full-operator CPTP maps and finite composition closure. The finite-composition formulation is the immediate iteration of the assigned binary composition theorem.
